sentences.text: This dinosaur was a small creature that reached lengths between 1.18 and 1.75 meters and weighed from 2 to 10 kilograms.
The most complete skeleton found measures about 1.18 meters long.
Two of the best-preserved skulls measure 108 mm and 121 mm in length.
Its head was small yet sturdy in build.
A young skull measuring just 45 mm suggests the animal grew to only 450 mm long as a juvenile.
Unlike many relatives, this species did not replace its teeth continuously throughout its life.
The species Heterodontosaurus tucki received its name in 1962 after a skull was found in South Africa.
That specific skull specimen was uncovered during a British-South African expedition between 1961 and 1962.
It was first described in 1962 as an early member of the order Ornithischia.
The genus name itself was coined by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
It is widely regarded as a plant-eating dinosaur.
Its unique jaws and teeth were specialized for processing vegetation with a complexity similar to later ornithischians.
Scientists believe it specialized in eating tough plants, while a related species likely consumed softer vegetation.
It possessed long arms with large, curved claws that could help it grab small prey.
Researchers suggest its strong arms were adapted for foraging, perhaps by digging up roots or breaking insect nests.
Although it was once thought to walk on four legs, it is now considered to have been bipedal.
Santa Luca proposed that the animal moved on four legs when slow but could switch to a faster two-legged run.
Its neck consisted of nine vertebrae that formed an S-shaped curve.
The teeth featured a thick enamel layer on the inside and had long roots securely anchored in their sockets.
Thulborn found no signs of continuous tooth replacement in known skulls, suggesting the teeth formed all at once.
He hypothesized that full tooth replacement happened only during aestivation, a time when the animal did not feed.
This dinosaur is the namesake and most famous member of the family Heterodontosauridae.
Sereno defined Heterodontosauridae as a clade in 1998 and 2005 based on skull traits like few premaxillary teeth, caniniform teeth, and a jugal horn.
It serves as the type and most well-known member of that family.
Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, roughly 200 to 190 million years ago.
Fossils are found in the Upper Elliot and Clarens Formations of the Karoo Supergroup, dating to the Lower Jurassic Hettangian and Sinemurian ages around 200 to 190 million years ago.
It inhabited what is now Africa during the Early Jurassic, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
Heterodontosaurids existed from the Late Triassic to the Early Cretaceous, spanning at least 100 million years.
In 1970, Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus.
Researchers suggest Heterodontosaurus may have had lip-like structures rather than bridging skin between the jaws.
In 1974, Thulborn suggested the tusks were likely used for combat, display, or defense rather than feeding.
In 2017, Matthew G. Baron and colleagues suggested grouping ornithischians with theropods in Ornithoscelida based on similarities between Heterodontosaurus and Eoraptor.
